newsitem.title: GERMANY: German regional jobless rate eases.
newsitem.headline: German regional jobless rate eases.

text.p: The number of jobless in the German state of North Rhine-Westphalia eased in May, falling 1.6 percent to 873,590, the state labour office said on Friday ahead of federal figures due at 0800 GMT.
The state's unadjusted unemployment rate of 11.0 percent, down from 11.1 percent in April, was almost identical to the rate expected for all of Germany.

Official sources on Thursday said May's pan-German joblessness on an unadjusted basis was 11.1 percent, with a total of 4.256 million Germans out of work. The unadjusted rate was 11.3 percent in April, with 4.347 million without work.

Meanwhile, the German Trade Union Federation (DGB) warned Bonn was heading toward a catastrophe if it did not release to the Federal Labour Office the 2.2 billion marks that have already been approved for job programmes.
Without retraining and job-creation money, Germany would see 150,000 more jobless by the end of 1997, DGB board member Ursula Engelen-Kefer told the Berliner Zeitung.
She added the drop in May's figures, as reported by the official source, was "completely insufficient."
"That is a seasonally typical reduction," she said. "And it should have fallen considerably more than that."
Engelen-Kefer repeated union calls for reducing the work week to 32 hours from 35, and cutting overtime by those already employed.
"Through that 30,000 jobs would be secured, and there would even be new additional jobs," she said.
